clue.text: Luxurious establishment on Piccadilly — it's a cracker!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the famous grand hotel on Piccadilly in London
second meaning: a brand of savoury biscuit, a cracker in the literal sense

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracker' reads as praise for the hotel (British slang for something excellent), but it is literal: the name is also a well-known brand of crackers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ritz is the landmark London hotel on Piccadilly, and Ritz is also a brand name for buttery snack biscuits.

clue.text: Wealthy creature around East German house

indicators.note: the word for wealthy goes around the letter for east, enclosing it

parts.note: rich means wealthy
E is the compass abbreviation for east
a stag is a male deer, a creature

explanation.surface: A rich animal living near a house in East Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' means a legislative house, not a home.
explanation.definitionFit: The Reichstag building in Berlin houses the Bundestag, Germany's parliament, a house of government.

clue.text: Scraps — skin of sausages left in fresh suet

indicators.note: these letters go inside the rearranged suet
fresh means new, so the letters of suet are made over into a new order
the skin is the outside, so the first and last letters of sausages

explanation.surface: Cooking scraps: sausage casings left lying in new suet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skin of sausages' gives SS; with L for left it goes inside TUES, a rearrangement of suet signalled by 'fresh'.
explanation.definitionFit: Scraps as a verb or noun means fights or scuffles, and tussles are rough struggles.

clue.text: One making new life abroad — former postman?

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife
Postman Pat, the children's TV postman

explanation.surface: A wry question whether an emigrant is a retired postman.
explanation.walkthrough: Postman Pat is a long-running British children's TV character, a village postman.
explanation.definitionFit: An expat is someone who has left their home country to settle and live overseas.

clue.text: Even-handed European who in Paris sits on board

indicators.note: in a down clue the earlier letters sit on top of the later ones

parts.note: qui is French for who
a board is a table, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A fair-minded European sits on a company board in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Equitable means fair and impartial, treating every side alike, which is even-handed.

clue.text: Spotted photo's source that is obvious

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it begins, its first letter

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
bald means plain and blunt, as in the bald truth

explanation.surface: Someone noticed where a photo came from, which was plain enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' reads as the verb noticed, but it is the adjective, patchy in colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A piebald horse has irregular black and white patches, so its coat is spotted.

clue.text: African expresses disapproval on island

parts.note: tuts means clicks the tongue in disapproval
I is the map abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: An African tutting at something on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tutsi are an ethnic group of Rwanda and Burundi in central Africa.

clue.text: Foxes skinned by northern cattle

indicators.note: a skinned word has its outer layer stripped, so the first and last letters of Foxes go

explanation.surface: Foxes being flayed by northern cattle farmers, a grim rural picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxen are domestic bovines, the plural of ox, so they are cattle used for draught work.

clue.text: Might such a vessel be well-filled?

definitions.text: Might such a vessel be well-filled?

parts.words: Might such a vessel be well-filled?
parts.note: a ship carrying the produce of a well, filled from an oil well rather than a water well

explanation.walkthrough: 'well-filled' sounds like fully loaded, but a well here is the kind drilled for petroleum.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a ship built to carry crude petroleum in bulk, the stuff pumped from wells.

clue.text: Beatles manager Brian records 'One In Ten'

parts.note: EPs are extended-play records

indicators.note: the letter for one goes within the word ten

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The Beatles' manager releases a record called One In Ten.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'One In Ten' look like a song title, but it is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Brian Epstein managed the Beatles from 1962 until his death in 1967.

clue.text: Fan must start in line to see player

indicators.note: to fan is to spread out, so the letters of the phrase are spread and rearranged

explanation.surface: An enthusiast has to queue from the start to see a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan' looks like a noun, a supporter, but it is a verb meaning spread out, the anagram signal over the next four words.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrumentalist is a musician who plays an instrument, so a player in the musical sense.

clue.text: Endlessly assist London force: copper's top!

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter of the word for assist is dropped

parts.note: to assist is to help
the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: A call to help the Metropolitan Police, ending on a policeman's headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' is a playful word for headwear: a British police officer's tall domed helmet.
explanation.definitionFit: A British constable traditionally wears a tall custodian helmet, the headgear a copper puts on.

clue.text: Lively friend protected by a new identity

indicators.note: the friend is shielded inside the identity, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: ID is short for identity, as on an ID card
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: A cheerful pal under witness protection with a fresh identity.
explanation.definitionFit: Animated describes someone full of life and spirit, so it is a synonym of lively.

clue.text: Sample an American beer — sensational thing!

parts.note: to sample food or drink is to taste it
Bud is short for Budweiser, an American lager

explanation.surface: Trying a US beer and finding it sensational.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sensational' sounds like praise for the beer, but it means to do with the senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A taste bud is a sensory organ on the tongue, literally a thing involved in sensation.

clue.text: Hotter MiG replaced British plane

indicators.note: placed again in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A faster Russian fighter jet took over from a British aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The de Havilland Tiger Moth is a 1930s British biplane trainer used by the RAF.

clue.text: Sun-worshipper in this atoll?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the two-piece swimsuit a sunbather would wear
second meaning: ... Atoll in the Marshall Islands

explanation.walkthrough: The swimsuit was named after the Pacific atoll where atomic tests took place, so the one word is both garment and place; the clue runs the two together.
explanation.definitionFit: A bikini is a skimpy two-piece swimsuit worn for sunbathing, and Bikini is also a Pacific atoll.

clue.text: Dancer likely to be up on points?

definitions.text: Dancer likely to be up on points?

parts.words: Dancer likely to be up on points?
parts.note: points here are the tips of the toes; a ballet dancer rises onto them, not ahead in a scoring contest

explanation.walkthrough: 'up on points' suggests leading a contest on points, but it means standing on the tips of the toes in ballet shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A female ballet dancer performs en pointe, balancing on the tips of her toes.

clue.text: Identical son in populous land where Jakarta lies

indicators.note: these letters are put inside the word for the populous land

parts.note: India, the world's most populous country
one, as in one and the same
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A twin son living in a crowded country around Jakarta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'populous land where Jakarta lies' looks like one definition, but 'populous land' is India in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Indonesia is the Southeast Asian archipelago nation whose capital city is Jakarta, on Java.

clue.text: Flock gathering at the edges in storm

indicators.note: the edge letters are placed inside the word for storm

parts.note: a gale is a storm-force wind

indicators.note: only the outermost letters of gathering are taken

explanation.surface: A flock of birds gathering at the edges of a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaggle is the collective noun for geese, a flock of them on the ground.

clue.text: Dilettante in a beaten RU team

indicators.note: something beaten is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dabbler playing in a defeated rugby union side.
explanation.walkthrough: RU stands for rugby union; here it is just two letters of the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur dabbles in an activity without professional skill, much as a dilettante does.

clue.text: Erudite elder in muddle with law

indicators.note: a muddle is a jumble, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A church elder confused about the law, despite being learned.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well-read has studied many books, so is scholarly and learned.

clue.text: Earn medal presented by king in castle

parts.note: to win something is to earn it
the DSO is the Distinguished Service Order, a British military award
R abbreviates rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone earns a medal handed over by the king inside his castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Windsor Castle in Berkshire is a royal residence, the oldest occupied castle in the world.

clue.text: Not a good look from these vile yeomen

indicators.note: the letters are drawn out of the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: These wicked yeomen give a nasty glare.
explanation.definitionFit: The evil eye is a malevolent glance believed to cause harm, certainly a bad look.

clue.text: Good Beatles guitarist leaving hotel for camp

indicators.note: the letter for hotel departs from the surname, so it is removed

parts.note: George Harrison, lead guitarist of the Beatles
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A Beatle checks out of his hotel for a campsite.
explanation.definitionFit: A garrison is the body of troops stationed at a military post, or the post itself, a camp.

clue.text: Mammals in ocean clash regularly

parts.note: the sea is the ocean

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter of clash is taken

explanation.surface: Marine mammals regularly fighting in the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Seals are marine mammals, flippered carnivores that live in the sea and haul out on land.

clue.text: Flag officer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a flag flown by a ship to show nationality
second meaning: a junior commissioned rank in the US Navy, or historically a standard-bearing officer

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a 'flag officer', a naval admiral, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is a naval flag and also the lowest commissioned rank in the US Navy.

clue.text: St John's view as he converted sectarian

indicators.note: converting changes the form of something, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Saint John's outlook after he was converted to a sect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' suits a religious surface perfectly, which hides its role as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jehovah's Witness belongs to a particular Christian denomination, so is a member of a sect.

clue.text: Roguish leader missing from demo

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, which goes missing

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

explanation.surface: A mischievous ringleader skips the demonstration.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch as an adjective means playfully mischievous or knowing, as in an arch smile.

clue.text: Shy artisan occasionally seen in country

indicators.note: only now and then, so every other letter of the words is taken

explanation.surface: A bashful craftsman is sometimes spotted in a foreign land.
explanation.definitionFit: Syria is a nation in the Middle East bordering Turkey, Iraq and Lebanon.

clue.text: Fine Greek character offers cheese

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A decent Greek fellow offering some cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests a person, but it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a white brined curd cheese from Greece made from sheep's or goat's milk.
